assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Electrolytic cell
items.clue: A DC power source drives a non-spontaneous redox reaction.

items.label: Hydride ion
items.clue: H⁻, the species that carries out the reduction of carbonyl compounds.

items.label: Salt bridge
items.clue: Connects two half-cells and lets ions move to keep the charge balanced.

items.label: Hydrogenation
items.clue: Addition of H₂ to an alkene or alkyne, lowering the degree of unsaturation.

questions.stem: What is the oxidation state of nitrogen in the ammonium ion, NH₄⁺?
questions.explanation: Each H is +1, contributing +4 in total. The oxidation states must add up to the ion's charge, +1: x + 4 = +1, so x = −3.

questions.stem: Which half-equation correctly shows the conversion of MnO₄⁻(aq) into Mn²⁺(aq) in acidic solution?
questions.explanation: O is balanced with 4H₂O, H with 8H⁺, and charge with electrons: left −1 + 8 − 5 = +2, right +2. Mn goes from +7 to +2, a gain of five electrons (reduction), so electrons are reactants.

questions.stem:
Chlorine reacts with aqueous iron(II) ions:
2Fe²⁺(aq) + Cl₂(aq) → 2Fe³⁺(aq) + 2Cl⁻(aq)
Which species is the oxidizing agent in this reaction?

options.text: Fe²⁺, since it loses electrons and so is itself oxidized
Cl₂, since it gains electrons and so is itself reduced
Cl⁻, since it is the species holding the gained electrons
None, since no species here gains or loses any oxygen atoms

questions.explanation: Chlorine's oxidation state falls from 0 to −1: each Cl₂ gains two electrons from Fe²⁺. The species that accepts electrons, and so is reduced, is the oxidizing agent.

questions.stem: In acidic solution, MnO₄⁻(aq) is reduced to Mn²⁺(aq) and Fe²⁺(aq) is oxidized to Fe³⁺(aq). In the balanced overall redox equation, what amount of Fe²⁺ reacts with 1 mol of MnO₄⁻?
questions.explanation: Manganese goes from +7 to +2, so each MnO₄⁻ gains 5 electrons (MnO₄⁻ + 8H⁺ + 5e⁻ → Mn²⁺ + 4H₂O); each Fe²⁺ loses 1. The iron half-equation is multiplied by 5: MnO₄⁻ + 8H⁺ + 5Fe²⁺ → Mn²⁺ + 4H₂O + 5Fe³⁺.
2(+1) + 2x + 7(−2) = 0 gives 2x = +12, so each Cr is +6: potassium dichromate(VI). The Roman numeral is the oxidation state of chromium, per atom.

questions.stem: Nitrogen has the oxidation state −3 in ammonia, NH₃. What is the oxidation state of nitrogen in the nitrate ion, NO₃⁻?
questions.explanation: O is −2, and the oxidation states must add up to the ion's charge: x + 3(−2) = −1, so x = +5. Like most main-group non-metals, nitrogen has variable oxidation states: −3 in NH₃, 0 in N₂, +4 in NO₂ and +5 in NO₃⁻.
